resolved_by: Amendment 827 (2024) moved intended loss from the commentary into the text of § 2B1.1(b)(1), and the majority held that the amendment is clarifying and applies to Horn's case. The concurrence does not decide whether the 2021 version was ambiguous.
issue: Under the 2021 Guidelines, does 'loss' in U.S.S.G. § 2B1.1(b)(1) include intended loss, or is the text ambiguous on that point, so that the commentary's inclusion of intended loss cannot be applied without more?

sides.position: 'Loss' in § 2B1.1(b)(1) is unambiguous and includes intended loss through § 1B1.3(a)(3).
cases: United States v. You, 74 F.4th 378 (6th Cir. 2023)
United States v. Jeffrey Alan Horn, 129 F.4th 1275 (11th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: 'Loss' in § 2B1.1(b)(1) is ambiguous, so intended loss cannot be applied on the 2021 text alone; § 1B1.3 adds ambiguity rather than resolving it.
cases: United States v. Banks, 55 F.4th 246 (3d Cir. 2022)
United States v. Boler, 115 F.4th 316 (4th Cir. 2024)

quote: Our sister circuits are divided on that question, compare United States v. You, 74 F.4th 378, 397–98 (6th Cir. 2023), with United States v. Banks, 55 F.4th 246, 258 (3d Cir. 2022), and the Fourth Circuit has concluded that § 2B1.1(b)(1) is ambiguous even after consulting § 1B1.3(a)(3).
cite: United States v. Jeffrey Alan Horn, 129 F.4th 1275 (11th Cir. 2025)
